package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious package or code is described in this report. The report analyzes the systemic risk in Sigstore's OIDC-based signing and validation model, especially in open ecosystems like PyPI or npm, where any user can create an account and sign packages. The threat is that malicious actors can use public OIDC providers to sign and distribute malicious packages, potentially misleading users and automated systems into trusting these packages based solely on the presence of a valid signature, without verifying the real-world identity or trustworthiness of the signer. No actual malicious package or code sample is analyzed.

behavioral_signatures: Packages signed with public OIDC provider identities (e.g., Google, GitHub, Microsoft) where the signer is not a known or trusted entity.
Presence of a valid signature on a package without additional verification of the signer's real-world identity or reputation.
New or unvetted maintainers signing packages using public OIDC providers, especially when the package is recently published or has no prior reputation.
file_indicators: No specific file indicators; the risk is associated with any package file (e.g., .whl, .tar.gz, .tgz) that is signed by an untrusted or unknown identity using a public OIDC provider.
network_indicators: No specific network indicators; the general risk involves the use of public OIDC providers (such as accounts.google.com, github.com, login.microsoftonline.com) for signing package metadata.
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Automated detection should not rely solely on the presence of a valid signature. Systems should verify the real-world identity and trustworthiness of the signer, correlating OIDC identities with known, reputable contributors or organizations. Flag packages signed by unknown, untrusted, or newly created OIDC identities, especially when the package is new or the maintainer has no established reputation. Implement additional controls to require manual review or enhanced scrutiny for packages signed by public OIDC providers where the signer's identity cannot be mapped to a trusted entity.
